methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells and cases are needed to test redistribution of initiations after an absence?
Which measures of play-type change and profile similarity are reliable at this sample size?
How should regression to the mean, usage confounding and selection of who is absent be handled in before-after comparisons?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether play-type replacement similarity separates absorption from cascade when a player sits. Recorded result: mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19, which the record calls wrong-signed. Recorded verdict: null, failure type B_powered_null. Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Absence validation: real absences move the association structure (V1) and the LOO simulation predicts the magnitude (V2). V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95 (binomial p=2.67e-16) and V1(b) +0.142 CI [+0.103, +0.187] were recorded as confirmed; V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] and V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115 failed. Limited by small sample.

Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence: paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96 matched pairs. Concerns team-level identity displacement, not which teammate gains.

On/off identity displacement: shaper absence displaces the team fingerprint more than a usage-matched non-shaper (Delta D_A=+0.115, t=6.35, p~7e-9, shaper larger in 81% of pairs; r(L,D_A)=+0.60). Concerns team-level fingerprint, not teammate-level gain allocation.

Routing possessions to each play type's best player (A5) vs baseline (A3) was tested as model-scored, not observed outcomes. Effect shrank from +0.94 pts/100 (V5) to +0.03 on 520 matchups (V6); A5b vs A5 -0.00. Verdict null, failure type B_powered_null. Relevant as a caution that best-player routing gains shrink with larger samples.

Connector presence shielding stars: star dTS +0.05 pp p=0.937; dTO +0.74 pp p=0.00364 (wrong sign for shielding); lineup on-off PPP both-null. Lineup ORtg lift was a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT). Verdict null, failure type B_powered_null.

Star suppression by lineup and forced play type (Jokic, Curry, Doncic, Giannis) descriptive gaps, e.g. Giannis forced PULL_UP 0.848 vs DRIVE gap -0.540. No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear.
Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock, 8/8 PTs replicated across all games and playoffs. Concerns sequential play-type effects, not absence redistribution.
Extended possession value: 4/8 play types show a real downstream opponent component (~0.01-0.02 PPP); DRIVE downstream not real. Player-level downstream mostly non-FINDING after BH correction.
Possession ending state vs next 90-180s volume/points, descriptive only; no inferential tests in core table.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type replacement similarity to predict which teammate absorbs versus cascades when a player sits.
failed_approaches.why: Similarity did not separate absorption from cascade (mean 0.863 vs 0.848) and the correlation was wrong-signed (Spearman -0.19). The record attributes this to B_powered_null, but the sample and power were NOT_RECORDED, so the 'adequately powered' label is not verifiable. The record also lists label or classification error as a limitation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Routing possessions to each play type's best player as a teammate-allocation rule.
failed_approaches.why: Effect shrank from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on the larger 520-matchup sample; recorded as B_powered_null. Results are model-scored, not observed outcomes.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of association-structure change under absence with a LOO simulation.
failed_approaches.why: V2a and V2b failed (CI spans zero), and the record marks the family untestable, limited by small sample.

evidence_establishes: Absence effects on team-level identity or fingerprint have been detected in earlier records (FAM:SF-APPS-088, FAM:SF-PAP-014), so absences are not without measurable structural effect.
Play-type similarity alone was not shown to predict which teammate absorbs or cascades (FAM:SF-CHT-052, recorded as null with a wrong-signed correlation).

Apparent best-player routing gains and connector effects shrank or vanished on larger samples or after confound control (FAM:SF-APPA-017, FAM:SF-APPS-087), which is a warning for single-teammate gainer claims.
Downstream and star-suppression findings in this project are small or descriptive without placebo control (FAM:SF-APPS-075, FAM:SF-CHT-009).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record directly tests whether the closest pre-absence-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types.
No retrieved record reports the number of cases or spells needed for that test, and FAM:SF-CHT-052 leaves sample and power unrecorded.
No retrieved record defines 'closest profile' operationally, or shows that the chosen similarity metric is reliable.
The retrieved records do not cover the 2025-26 partial-season data version or its effect on the sample.
Whether teammate-level gains are distinguishable from regression to the mean and usage reallocation is not established.
own_inferences: With 11 cases, a teammate-level ranking test (closest profile versus all other teammates) has very few independent units, so any result is likely to be dominated by one or two spells.

The 'most minutes' or 'most initiations' fallback criterion is close to mechanical: teammates with the most minutes or usage will tend to gain the most initiations after a high-usage player sits, which would make a positive result partly an artifact.
FAM:SF-CHT-052 is the closest prior test and its wrong-signed result suggests the similarity-to-gainer link is unlikely to hold, though its unrecorded power limits how much weight a null can carry.
Defining 'closest profile' with the same play-type shares used to define 'primary types' would make the result partly circular.
uncertainties: The sample sizes behind FAM:SF-CHT-052 and FAM:SF20 are not recorded in the returned fields.
The definition of 'closest profile' (distance metric, feature set, and whether it uses pre-absence data only) is not given in the task.
The definition of 'primary types', the threshold for 'largest gainer', and the handling of ties are not specified.
Whether the 148 spells overlap for the same players across seasons, and how many distinct absent players there are, is not given; the 11-case figure may be the effective unit count.
The 2025-26 regular season and playoff data are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, so the analysis cut must be fixed before any run.
Whether the play-by-play-derived initiator records classify play types reliably (label error) is not established by the retrieved records.

historical_effect.explanation: Prior work (FAM:SF-CHT-052) found that similarity did not predict absorption versus cascade, with a wrong-signed correlation, and FAM:SF-APPA-017 showed best-player routing gains shrinking on larger samples. Together with the 11-case design, these records move the decision from a confirmatory test to do_not_proceed. Only a descriptive or minimum viable analysis is justified. The retrieved records do not directly answer the question, so the decision rests on the closest precursor's null and the sample constraint, not on a settled answer.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 cases (148 spells) is too few independent units to rank teammates and detect a closest-profile gainer effect; the closest precursor (FAM:SF-CHT-052) left power unrecorded.
Teammates with the most minutes or initiations gain the most by default, so a positive result is expected even without a profile effect.
Primary-type and initiator labels come from play-by-play derived records; FAM:SF-CHT-052 lists label or classification error as a limitation.
Gains are measured on play-type initiation shares derived from the same outcome records used to define primary types.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the closest-profile teammate as largest gainer. FAM:SF-CHT-052 tested the nearest precursor (similarity separating absorption from cascade) and found no signal, with a wrong-signed correlation and unrecorded power. FAM:SF20 found only partial support for absence-driven structure change and failed its magnitude validation. FAM:SF-APPS-088 and FAM:SF-PAP-014 support team-level identity displacement but not teammate-level gain allocation. The question is therefore only partly addressed by precursors.

risks.text: 11 cases and 148 spells give little power for a teammate-ranking test with multiple candidates.
The minutes or initiations fallback ranks high-usage teammates first by construction, so gainer status is partly mechanical.
Largest absolute gain scales with a teammate's baseline usage, so the closest-profile test may be confounded with teammate size.
Absences selected by injury or unusual usage spikes may show regression to the mean, inflating gains for teammates with low baseline shares.
Position, role, minutes and lineup context co-vary with profile similarity and with gains; no control is specified.
Initiator and play-type labels from play-by-play may be misclassified, and FAM:SF-CHT-052 lists this as a limitation.
Primary types and gains may be defined from the same outcome data, which makes the test partly circular.
Profile similarity from a few hundred initiations per player may be unstable, and the metric is unspecified.
Many play types have few initiations per teammate per spell, so gain estimates are noisy and zero-inflated.
Testing every teammate, play type and season separately inflates false positives.
Seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26 differ in pace and play-type mix, and 2025-26 is partial before its cut dates.
Partial 2025-26 data before 2026-04-13 (regular season) and 2026-06-21 (playoffs) could leak post-absence information if the cut is not fixed in advance.
Without a placebo (non-absence games or non-absent teammates), gains may reflect general usage shifts rather than absence.

design.estimand: As a minimum viable test: the difference in change in the absent player's primary play-type initiation share between the teammate with the closest pre-absence profile and the highest-minutes teammate, versus all other teammates, across absence spells. This is descriptive unless the sample is expanded.
design.unit: Absence spell (one absent player, one season window), with each candidate teammate as a sub-unit; cluster by absent player.
design.sample: Available data: 11 cases, 148 spells, NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs. Use only seasons complete at the cut date; exclude partial 2025-26 data unless the cut is fixed at 2026-04-13 (regular season) and 2026-06-21 (playoffs).
design.power: Not adequate for a confirmatory test with 11 cases. A minimum detectable effect cannot be stated from the recorded data, so report effect sizes with bootstrap CIs at the case level and do not claim support from a single case.
design.controls: Pre-absence teammate usage and minutes, position, lineup context, and a usage-matched placebo (teammates of the same usage tier in non-absence windows). Regression to the mean handled by using pre-absence windows for profile and post-absence windows for gains, with a within-player baseline.
design.falsification: Pre-registered wrong-sign check as in FAM:SF-CHT-052: if the closest-profile teammate's gain is no larger than the placebo teammate's gain, or the mean similarity-gain correlation is negative, the hypothesis is rejected. Also check that the minutes-based fallback does not explain the result.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across play types and teammate ranks; the primary test is one pre-specified comparison (closest-profile versus highest-minutes teammate).
design.decision_rule: Support only if the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in a pre-specified primary play type in a majority of cases, with a case-level bootstrap CI excluding zero and the usage-matched placebo beaten. Otherwise report as null or inconclusive. Do not proceed to confirmatory claims at 11 cases.
design.data_version: NBA play-by-play for 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular season and playoffs (complete); 2025-26 regular season only if the cut is 2026-04-13 or later, and 2025-26 playoffs only if the cut is 2026-06-21 or later. Freeze the data version and the definition of 'closest profile' before running.

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many spells and cases are needed to test redistribution of initiations after an absence?
Which measures of play-type change are reliable at this sample size?
How should regression to the mean and selection effects be handled in absence-based before-after comparisons?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
